title: eBPF instruction (8 bytes)
summary: An eBPF program is a sequence of 8-byte instructions. Each instruction: 1-byte opcode (class + op), 1-byte dst/src registers (4 bits each), 2-byte offset (signed), 4-byte immediate. Classes: 0 LD, 1 LDX, 2 ST, 3 STX, 4 ALU, 5 JMP, 6 JMP32, 7 ALU64.

ext.summary: An eBPF program is a sequence of 8-byte instructions. Each instruction: 1-byte opcode (class + op), 1-byte dst/src registers (4 bits each), 2-byte offset (signed), 4-byte immediate. Classes: 0 LD, 1 LDX, 2 ST, 3 STX, 4 ALU, 5 JMP, 6 JMP32, 7 ALU64.

structure.meaning: Destination register (r0-r10; r10 is read-only frame pointer).
Immediate value; for 64-bit loads, a second instruction carries the high 32 bits.

ext.example_decoded: r1 += 42 (ALU64 ADD immediate): opcode 0x07, dst r1, src 0, off 0, imm 42
notes: 11 registers: r0 (return value), r1-r5 (args), r6-r9 (callee-saved), r10 (frame pointer, read-only).
eBPF programs are verified by the kernel's BPF verifier before execution (no unbounded loops, bounded memory access, type safety).
Maps are key-value stores shared between BPF programs and userspace.
BPF programs attach to kprobes, tracepoints, XDP, cgroup, socket filters, LSM hooks, etc.
Classic BPF (cBPF) is the older 32-bit filter format used by seccomp and tcpdump; eBPF is the modern 64-bit VM.
